title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Prohibiting Current Judges from Serving as Arbitrators
full_text_en:
Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Prohibiting Judges in Active Service from Serving as Arbitrators

Fa [2004] No. 129

To all High People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Recently, the Supreme People's Court has responded to inquiries from deputies to the National People's Congress regarding whether judges may be appointed by arbitration commissions to serve as arbitrators. The relevant principles are hereby notified as follows:

In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China and the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China, it is inconsistent with the applicable laws for judges to serve as arbitrators and engage in the arbitration of cases. Such conduct exceeds the scope of functions and powers of the People's Courts and judges, and is detrimental to the impartial protection of the lawful rights and interests of litigation parties in accordance with the law. Therefore, judges shall not serve as arbitrators. Any judge who has already been appointed by an arbitration commission to serve as an arbitrator shall resign from the position of arbitrator and terminate the appointment relationship within one month after the issuance of this Notice.

This Notice is hereby given.

July 13, 2004
